title: The proper-support Quot presheaf of a quasi-coherent module
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:A\to B$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Use the chartwise and topological morphism properties of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; a morphism is of finite presentation if it is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with quasi-separated meaning quasi-compact diagonal. A closed immersion is representable and a closed immersion on scheme base changes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Modules, quasi-coherence and tensor pullback are on the small etale ringed sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is of finite presentation if etale locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. Use the stalkwise relative flatness convention of [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] on each etale scheme chart. A module on $A_T=A\times_BT$ is flat over a scheme $T$ if, on each etale scheme chart $U\to A_T$, its stalk at every $u\in U$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t(u)}$ through $U\to T$. It has support proper over $T$ if there exist a closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow A_T$ proper over $T$ and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq M$; finite type for modules means etale locally finitely generated. Assume $a$ is of finite presentation and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_A$-module. Define $\operatorname{Quot}_{\mathcal F/A/B}(T)$ for each scheme $T\to B$ to be the set of isomorphism classes of surjections $q:\mathcal F_T\twoheadrightarrow Q$, where $\mathcal F_T$ is tensor pullback along $A_T\to A$, and $Q$ is quasi-coherent, of finite presentation, flat over $T$, and has support proper over $T$. Two surjections are identified if an isomorphism of their target modules intertwines them. For $T\prime\to T$ the transition is tensor pullback of the surjection along $A_{T\prime}\to A_T$. For every scheme $T\to B$ the projection $A_T\to T$ is locally of finite type: choose a surjective etale chart $V\to B$ and a surjective etale chart $U\to A\times_BV$; the chart map $U\to V$ of $a$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type; with $V_T=V\times_BT$, the pair $U\times_VV_T\to A_T\times_TV_T$, $V_T\to T$ is again a pair of surjective etale charts [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], its chart map $U\times_VV_T\to V_T$ is a base change of $U\to V$ and so locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], and one such pair of charts suffices [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. Hence, applied to $A_T\to T$ and $T\prime\to T$, [lem-sfb-space-module-base-change-flat-proper-support] shows that the target conditions are preserved. Transitions use the canonical tensor-pullback identification $(\mathcal F_T)_{T'}\simeq\mathcal F_{T'}$; identity and composition are taken on isomorphism classes via the tensor unit and associativity identifications. This defines the proper-support Quot presheaf on schemes over $B$.
